Feed-back to BBS (papers/bbs/REVIEW.md §H.2, POSTWAVE5/BBS-NOTES.md (3)): the construction there — 1·(r,θ,z) = (r‖g w(θ)‖/‖w(ĝθ+2πm)‖, ĝθ+2πm, z) with w a 2π-periodic Euclidean parametrisation — does not give a Hausdorff quotient, because the action rescales the Euclidean radius while 𝔻_∞'s apex neighbourhoods are {r < ε}: for the tachyon the quotient is not even T₁ (a point of the contracted eigen-ray lies in every neighbourhood of an axis point, GX.rayLiftQuotient_tachyon_not_t1, every β ≠ 0, every m), for the photon it is not T₂ (p_n = (−1/(s²n²), 1/(sn), 0) → (apex, 0) while φⁿp_n = (−1/(s²n²), 0, 1) → (apex, 1), GX.rayLiftQuotient_photon_not_t2, every s ≠ 0, every m). §H.2 checks only the neighbourhood half (hdisc) of proper discontinuity, which holds. The fix is to make the action preserve r: choose w equivariant (w(ĝθ + 2πm) = g w(θ), defined on a fundamental domain and extended), equivalently act on θ alone.

For the photon no complement of ℝv is invariant under a null rotation, so in the Euclidean-radius reading the action must also shift z ((r,θ,z) ↦ (r‖Ae^{iθ}‖, θ + rayShift A θ + 2πm, z + r κ(e^{iθ}))); BBS H.2's z-preserving formula holds only for the tachyon. In the corrected reading the drift is absorbed in the developing map (the term r b(θ) c v).

Every element of Isom₀ fixing a spacelike (resp. null) line pointwise is a boost (resp. a null rotation): the orientation-reversing candidates (exchange of the two null lines of v^⊥; γ = −1 for the null case) are excluded only by the determinant condition of Isom₀.

l.679 names no lift of the PSL(2,ℝ) element to \widetilde{RP¹}: the lift is a choice m ∈ ℤ of sheets. Every m ≠ 0 is certified (m = ±1 the tachyon/photon proper); m = 0 (the lift fixing the eigen-rays) is not claimed.

WP-41r: Antoine's lemma for every generation is reduced, sorry-free, to its first generation (GX.antoineMeridianEssentialTop_of_firstGeneration): the classical van Kampen argument (incompressible boundary tori, amalgamated products) is formalized through a topological SvK theorem built for the purpose (GX.VanKampen.homotopicIn_of_homotopicIn_union', no path-connectedness of U, V needed) and mathlib's Monoid.PushoutI.of_injective; the induction must carry ALL powers of the meridian (the collar's injectivity on the tube side needs m^a non-null for every a != 0).

WP-41r round 1: the first generation is reduced, sorry-free, to its non-abelian heart (GX.antoineFirstGeneration_of_chain). The five collar facts are proved: the round tubes miss the other links (non-consecutive pairs box-separated by decide, consecutive ones by GX.antoine_tube_aux; the corner-diagonal pairs ARE box-separated once the tube's bounds are strict, so the round-tube argument is needed only for consecutive pairs); the base points are joined by explicit polygonal paths certified by decide; and the collar is path-connected, and is classified by two windings (GX.antoine_collar_classify, pi_1(T^2 x I) = Z^2 through a retraction onto the torus |W| = 3/14 and a straight-line homotopy of lifted angles), the longitudinal winding being read in S^3 \ C_1 through the next link, around which the longitude of link j winds +-1 (GX.antoine_succ_wind, by free homotopies in C \ 0, GX.AntoineLiftWind.of_freeHomotopy).

Hand computation (not formalized; recorded for the next package): the meridian of L is detected in S^3 \ C_1 by a D_inf = Z/2 * Z/2 representation (a Fox Z-colouring of the necklace diagram), sending it to a translation of infinite order; so a METABELIAN invariant suffices at the first generation, while no fixed solvable invariant works for all generations (the meridian lies in the k-th derived subgroup of pi_1(S^3 \ C_k)) -- which is why the reduction to the first generation is needed.

WP-41r round 2: Antoine's lemma at the first generation (GX.AntoineChainEssential) is proved with no Fox calculus and no presentation of pi_1: let P = prod over the 32 vertical links of Theta'_i (Theta_i or its conjugate on the sides y = -7/8, x = -7/8) and N the slab |tau| < 1e-4 around the sphere {z = 0} u {inf}, outside the closed holes of the 32 horizontal links. On N, R = chi * prod sqrt(Theta'_i) is a continuous square root of P (chi = -1 inside the core square): the principal roots are cut exactly in the 32 gaps of the chain, and there the side chi flips with them (sign(Im w) sqrt w = i sqrt(-w)); elsewhere chi is locally constant because in the slab the core square is covered by the closed holes and the gaps. The invariant exp(i pi (s/R) phi(tau)) on the double cover s^2 = P winds 2 along the meridian (it crosses the slab outside and inside the core square, on opposite sheets) and 0 along a null-homotopy. The closing of the chain enters exactly once: inside and outside of the core square meet in N only through the gaps; deleting link 8 opens a passage with no cut and R is no longer continuous, matching the fact that the meridian then bounds.

statements.label: prop:quotient_chart
paper_findings: No proof is printed (the ledger row is 'open'). The proof here: D : (cylinder, T_BTZ) -> (J+(Delta), BTZ) is a homeomorphism (GX.btzJDevHomeomorph): continuity because D^{-1}(I+(p_s) u ]p_s,+inf[) = {s < t + kappa r} is naturally open; openness at the axis from the estimate GX.btz_axis_diamond (the set I-(P_eta) n (I+(p_{t-eta}) u ]p_{t-eta},+inf[) pulls back into the horn neighbourhood {r(1+theta^2) < eps, |t'-t| < eps}); D is Gamma-equivariant and T_BTZ induces the quotient topology of E_0 (coinduced_orbitMk_tamTop), so D-bar is a homeomorphism; on regular parts both charts are translates of D.
With the BTZ topology Gamma\J+(Delta) is Hausdorff (GX.btzJQuot_instances), in contrast with the quotient of the usual topology (l.2273).

The paper does not say which singular E^{1,2}-structure Gamma\J+(Delta) carries (l.2286-2289). It is forced, not a reading: the regular part Gamma\(J+(Delta)\Delta) is the quotient of an open subset of E^{1,2} by a free, properly discontinuous group of isometries, and the singular structure extending it making the projection an a.e. morphism is unique (prop:aeGXquotient; GX.btzJQuot_existsUnique). That structure is the one used (AUDIT-2 minor: moved from questions to findings).

The proof's 'S_x is a totally ordered relatively open future half line, so is its image' (l.2385–2386) needs a BTZ point strictly below each BTZ point on its developed line; proved (btzTilde_exists_sing_below) through one descending chart along the full future BTZ ray of p(x) started slightly in the past of p(x) — the openness of the domain W of the ray's E₀-morphism.

WP-47g fixer (audit major 1): the proof's identification l.2390–2395 ('the image of such D(I_{p,q}) together with the topology induced by M generates the BTZ topology on D(M~)') is PROVED: GX.BTZTildeData.btzRangeTop_eq_devImageTop — defi:BTZtop traced on D(M~) near the rays (GX.btzRangeTop) equals the topology generated by M3 and the D-images of T_BTZ-opens.
